clue.text: The Times unmentioned in Tit-bits flyer

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time; here every T is meant

indicators.note: what goes unmentioned is left out, so every letter standing for time is dropped from the word

parts.note: taken as written, without the hyphen

explanation.surface: A newspaper columnist grumbles that their paper got no mention in the rival magazine Tit-Bits.
explanation.walkthrough: Take all three Ts out of TITBITS and IBIS is left. Tit-Bits was a popular British weekly magazine, and The Times a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading bird, so it is a flyer in the general crossword sense of a bird.

clue.text: Something enchanting from poet in steps of rare praise

indicators.note: walking in steps lands on every second spot, so only alternate letters are taken

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

explanation.surface: A tribute in verse moves through stages of unusual admiration.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at 'of', not 'rare': the even letters of 'of rare praise' spell the word. The word is the old poetic spelling famous from Spenser's The Faerie Queene.
explanation.definitionFit: Faerie is the archaic literary form for fairyland or a fairy, a magical thing found in poetry such as Spenser.

clue.text: In which, fixated by notable date, am I not deluded about love?

definitions.text: In which, fixated by notable date, am I not deluded about love?

indicators.note: something fixated by another is held fast within it, so the remaining letters sit inside
the jumble goes around the next item, wrapping it

parts.note: an era is a period dated from a notable event

indicators.note: a deluded mind has its thoughts scrambled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Someone obsessed with an anniversary asks whether they are really mistaken about romance.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange AM I NOT around O to get OTOMANI, then put that inside ERA. The whole clue also describes the condition: a deluded belief about love.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotomania is the delusion that another person is in love with you, a state in which one is deluded about love.

clue.text: Cut a slice of Somerset (or Dorset??) Cheddar

parts.note: surface padding: the other county, which would hide the same letters

indicators.note: a slice is a piece taken from within something larger, so the letters lie inside the words

parts.note: found running across the county name and the cheese

explanation.surface: Instructions to cut a piece of West Country cheese, with doubt over which county it comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that it hides equally well in 'Somerset Cheddar' and 'Dorset Cheddar', hence the bemused question marks. Both are English counties.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to cut lines into a surface, so etched is a past-tense synonym for cut in engraving.

clue.text: Receive news about article made of tanned hide

indicators.note: the first word goes around the following one, enclosing it

parts.note: to learn something is to receive news of it
the definite article

explanation.surface: A report on an item fashioned from cured animal skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Leathern is an old adjective describing things made of leather, which is tanned animal hide.

clue.text: More than 50% of the letters above

wordplay.note: the alphabet from its first letter through to the sixteenth, which is over half of twenty-six

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what proportion of the characters sit higher up the page.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'A to P' as a stretch of the alphabet: sixteen of the twenty-six letters, so more than half.
explanation.definitionFit: Atop is a preposition meaning on top of, which serves exactly as above does in a sentence.

clue.text: A fall in teaching of old French region

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: lore is a body of teaching or traditional knowledge
rain is a fall from the sky

explanation.surface: A collapse in education standards in a historic province of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorraine is a historical province in north-eastern France, now part of the Grand Est region.

clue.text: Take once-a-year drinker out, maybe to the Stars in Ely, getting tiddly

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside it
tiddly means tipsy, and a tipsy word staggers into a new order

parts.note: the cathedral city, taken as written
Latin for to the stars, as in the RAF motto per ardua ad astra

explanation.surface: Taking a teetotaller to a pub called the Stars in Ely, where they end up a little drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Stars' looks like a pub name, but it must be translated into Latin. Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire; 'tiddly' is British slang for slightly drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead astray is to tempt someone into misbehaving, as taking a rare drinker out boozing might, hence the 'maybe'.

clue.text: This Libya-Ireland passage?

indicators.note: a passage is a section lifted from a text, so the letters lie within the words

parts.note: found across the join of the two country names

explanation.surface: A query about a journey between North Africa and Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden letters also describe how such a journey would most likely be made, so the clue doubles as its own definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling by air means flying, the obvious way to make a passage from Libya to Ireland.

clue.text: Time to reject Old Year — insert this by end of date

definitions.meaning: surface reading: the moment to cast off the year just ending

definitions.text: insert this by end of date
definitions.meaning: setter's reading: the number now written at the end of every date in the new year

explanation.surface: New Year advice: time to throw out the old year and write the new figures when dating things.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared at the start of 2021, so from now on the year's last two digits change from 20 to this number.
explanation.definitionFit: In 2021 the final two digits written in every date became 21, the figure one adds at the end of the date.

clue.text: Some time, this compiler's beginnings in Hatfield perhaps, looking back

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside it
looking back means facing the other way, so the place name is read from its end

parts.note: Hatfield is a town in Hertfordshire, abbreviated Herts; 'perhaps' marks an example

indicators.note: beginnings are the starts of words, so only each first letter is kept

parts.note: the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: The setter reminisces about their early days in Hatfield.
explanation.walkthrough: Hertfordshire is an English county just north of London. Reverse its abbreviation, then slot the two initials in before the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch is a continuous period, and in slang a prison sentence, so it means some time.

clue.text: Cart-horse bureaucracy, up to a point?

indicators.note: putting the cart before the horse swaps rear and front, so the back part moves to the front

parts.note: red tape is bureaucratic procedure

explanation.surface: Officialdom about a working horse, accepted only partly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up to a point' looks like a hedge meaning partly; read literally it describes something narrowing to a point.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tapered narrows gradually until it ends in a point, which is the literal sense of the phrase.

clue.text: This man features in weird sleep

indicators.note: to feature in something is to appear within it

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or weird
the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man appears in a strange dream while asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleep' is not slumber here but the crust that forms in the corners of the eyes overnight. 'Rum' meaning odd is British.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is the watery discharge from eyes that dries as the crusty matter people call sleep.

clue.text: Have you just made one on your completed grid?

definitions.meaning: surface reading: a New Year pledge you have just made
setter's reading: a finished puzzle is solved, and solving is another sense of the word

explanation.surface: A New Year question asked of a solver who has just finished this crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a firm New Year pledge and the act of solving a problem, as a completed grid shows.

clue.text: It's tied up with restrictions of cuisine

definitions.text: It's tied up with restrictions of cuisine

indicators.note: something tied up is churned up and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: restrictions are bounds, so only the outer edges of the word are taken

parts.note: the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A field that is bound up with limits on what we may eat.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the subject: a discipline concerned with restricting food.
explanation.definitionFit: Dietetics is the science of diet and nutrition, which deals in controlling and limiting what people eat.

clue.text: Counteracting unfair treatment, Jolson leaves Ross early 20thC collection

indicators.note: counteracting works against something, turning it the opposite way
the singer leaves, so his name departs from the phrase

parts.note: a raw deal is unfair treatment
Al Jolson, the American singer
Diana Ross, the American singer

explanation.surface: A tale of justice being done as one singer quits another's company.
explanation.walkthrough: Take AL out of RAW DEAL, turn the rest round, then add Ross's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwardiana are objects and memorabilia from the Edwardian era, the reign of Edward VII from 1901 to 1910.

clue.text: Welcome 20 10, did you say? Enter here to make merry with wine and no end of beer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: greet twenty twenty-one, spoken from the figures plus the answers at 20 and 10

definitions.text: Enter here to make merry with wine and no end of beer
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a description of a party on 31 December

explanation.walkthrough: Say '20' then the answer at 10 and you hear twenty twenty-one, the year being welcomed when this puzzle ran.
explanation.definitionFit: To welcome a coming year is to celebrate its arrival at midnight, usually with drink and festivity.

clue.text: Music centre at which ____'s played?

indicators.note: played suggests letters performed in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asks what is played at a music venue, with a blank where the act should be.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank stands for the gap in a show: the music is played in the middle, when nothing else is happening on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: An entr'acte is music performed in the interval between two acts of a play or opera.

clue.text: Meanly keep mum — no time to 16!

parts.note: to hog is to keep selfishly
an informal word for mother
an old word for no

explanation.surface: A miser stays silent and has no time to celebrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep mum' looks like a phrase meaning stay quiet, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogmanay is the Scottish name for New Year's Eve, the occasion to welcome the year with a party.

clue.text: Slow glacier moving round this is not detected

indicators.note: the jumble goes round the next item, enclosing it
a moving thing shifts position, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word 'is' goes undetected, meaning those letters are dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A glacier creeps along so slowly that nobody notices it moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargic describes someone sluggish and lacking energy, so slow is a fair adjective synonym.

clue.text: A bit of Christmas cheer's unusual around nursery

indicators.note: the jumble goes around the single letter, enclosing it
an unusual form is an altered one, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: just a bit of the word is used, namely its first letter

parts.note: the first letter

explanation.surface: Festive goodwill is rare around the children's nursery at Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites the nativity crib, another sense of the word, but the definition here is the childcare one.
explanation.definitionFit: A crèche is a nursery where young children are looked after while their parents work or shop.

clue.text: Received summons notice with some style!

indicators.note: something received by the ear is heard, so the pieces are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: a writ is a legal summons, and to see is to notice

explanation.surface: Someone served with a court summons takes the news with flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Received' looks like part of the story of being served, but it signals sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritzy, from the Ritz hotel, means showily smart and luxurious, so it describes something done with style.

clue.text: Shake what took over a day to build right up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

parts.words: what took over a day to build
parts.note: from the saying that Rome was not built in a day
a standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Shaking something that took ages to put together.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor is a shaking movement, as of the ground or a hand, so the noun fits shake.

clue.text: NZ resident clipped car reversing back over something suspicious

indicators.note: a reversing car goes backwards, so its letters run backwards
something clipped has its end trimmed off

parts.note: auto is a car

indicators.note: turning back over flips the order of the letters

parts.note: from the phrase to smell a rat

explanation.surface: A New Zealander backs a damaged car over something dubious.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuatara is a lizard-like reptile found only in New Zealand, so it is a native resident there.

clue.text: Justify what one's done with eggs on the turn?

indicators.note: something on the turn is turning round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with
ova are eggs

explanation.surface: Defending one's cooking when the eggs have started to go off.
explanation.walkthrough: Turn W and OVA round together.
explanation.definitionFit: To avow is to declare openly and stand by an action, owning it rather than denying it.

clue.text: Out-door clothes dope's pressing

indicators.note: to clothe something is to wrap it up, so one word encloses the next

parts.note: an exit is a door leading out
dope and gen are both slang for information

explanation.surface: Garments for outdoors are urgently needed, says a drug user.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' looks like a noun in the surface but is a verb here. Gen is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Exigent means urgent and demanding immediate attention, just as a pressing matter does.

clue.text: Official figures hot parts still rising

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading upwards, so backwards
the hot item parts the next word, splitting it to sit inside

parts.note: still and yet both mean nevertheless or up to now
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Government statistics show temperatures still climbing in some regions.
explanation.definitionFit: They is the faceless authority in sayings like 'they say', the officials who run things.

clue.text: Manipulating sort thought a poet's odes retro features

indicators.note: retro means backward-looking, so the letters are read from right to left
what a phrase features it contains, so the letters lie within these words

parts.note: running from the end of the first word into the last

explanation.surface: A scheming type considered that a poet's verses were old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manipulating sort' suggests a schemer, but the manipulation is of bones and joints.
explanation.definitionFit: An osteopath treats patients by manipulating the bones, muscles and joints with the hands.

clue.text: What's left of energy after twelve, and who's got any?

parts.note: noon is twelve o'clock midday

indicators.note: the left end of a word is its start, so the first letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter

explanation.surface: Wondering who still has any energy left after midnight celebrations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's left of' sounds like a remnant but means the leftmost letter. 'After' places it behind the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Asked who has any, the answer is nobody, so the pronoun phrase replies to the question.
